source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR03 campus in Hillsboro occupies 182,000 square feet of technical space. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this facility, so no IT load, critical load, or total power capacity appears on its spec page. Without a published power number, it is not possible to estimate rack count or accelerator density, and POR03 does not contribute to Oregon's published capacity total.

Because no megawatt figure is published, POR03 ranks seventh among Oregon facilities by published power on this site, which is a way of saying it falls outside the six facilities that have published any number at all. Oregon has 133 mapped facilities in total, six of which have published a megawatt figure, summing to 182 MW across the state. POR03's 182,000 square feet is a substantial footprint, but square footage alone cannot be converted to power capacity without assuming a power density, and no such assumption is warranted here because the operator has provided no anchor figure.

For a reader evaluating AI relevance, the missing power number is the central fact. A facility of this floor area could, in principle, support a meaningful portion of AI workloads if built to modern densities, but that is speculation. What is published is space. What determines AI capacity is power. Until Stack Infrastructure publishes a critical load or total power figure for POR03, this campus cannot be placed on the compute-to-grid chain that determines AI scaling potential.
